load_basis: Operator-stated load capacity (an Equinix spokesperson told Bisnow, 2024-12-04, that the building 'has a 30-MW load capacity'); capacity, not metered draw
notes: Largest data center found in Florida. 50 NE 9th St, six stories, about 750,000 sq ft; built by Terremark, opened 2001, sold by Verizon to Equinix (deal announced 2016). Coordinates: U.S. Census geocoder match on the operator-published street address. A 2018 fifth-floor phase added 4 MW of UPS-backed power (https://datacenterknowledge.com/networking/equinix-expands-miami-data-center-that-s-key-to-latin-american-connectivity). The 30 MW is capacity: FPL's own count puts ALL 62 data center accounts on its system at about 32 average MW in 2024, so actual draw here is likely well under 30 MW. Utility is a territory inference only (Florida PSC approximate IOU service-area map; no operator, utility or docket source names the supplier for this building), hence low confidence and arrangement unknown. Context from the Florida PSC 2025 Ten-Year Site Plan review, Table 3 (https://floridapsc.com/pscfiles/website-files/PDF/Utilities/Electricgas/TenYearSitePlans/2025/Review.pdf): FPL identified 62 existing data center accounts using 283.0 GWh in 2024 (about 32 average MW in total, 30.2 MW summer-peak impact), and the PSC calls Florida's existing data centers 'relatively small'. Equinix's own site pages returned 403 and were not used. Our inventory carries 15.8 MW for this fid.

2100 NW 84th Ave, Doral; freestanding purpose-built facility of 103,000+ sq ft. CoreSite completed its acquisition on 2022-09-27 (https://www.coresite.com/news/coresite-expands-in-miami-completes-acquisition-of-state-of-the-art-data-center); seller, original build year and MW are not stated in any operator document fetched, so year and load stay null. Our inventory's 21 MW for this fid could not be verified and looks high against FPL's system-wide figure. Utility is a territory inference only (Florida PSC approximate IOU service-area map; no operator, utility or docket source names the supplier for this building), hence low confidence and arrangement unknown. Context from the Florida PSC 2025 Ten-Year Site Plan review, Table 3 (https://floridapsc.com/pscfiles/website-files/PDF/Utilities/Electricgas/TenYearSitePlans/2025/Review.pdf): FPL identified 62 existing data center accounts using 283.0 GWh in 2024 (about 32 average MW in total, 30.2 MW summer-peak impact), and the PSC calls Florida's existing data centers 'relatively small'. Coordinates: U.S. Census geocoder match on the operator-published street address.

9701 S. John Young Parkway (unincorporated Orange County per Census geocoder); 129,000+ sq ft on 16 acres. Legacy DataSite facility: American Tower acquired DataSite in 2021 and the building was upgraded and rebranded CoreSite OR1 in 2022, so our inventory's 2023 start year is NOT the first-operation year; the original opening year was not found, so left null. No MW figure in the operator page, spec sheet or market brochure (brochure notes a 'Twin Plant' power configuration and 30,000+ sq ft of expansion space); our 12.6 MW is unverified. Serving utility not determined: the site is in an area where Duke Energy Florida and OUC territories meet, and no source names the supplier. Context: OUC reported no existing data centers to the PSC, and Duke Energy Florida reported 5 totaling 48.0 GWh in 2024 (https://floridapsc.com/pscfiles/website-files/PDF/Utilities/Electricgas/TenYearSitePlans/2025/Review.pdf). Coordinates: U.S. Census geocoder match on the operator-published street address.

load_basis: Built critical capacity: operator spec sheet lists UPS capacity 2.5 MW (utility capacity 9 MW, generator capacity 9 MW, 19,245 sq ft raised floor)
notes: 9310 Florida Palm Drive, Tampa 33619 (unincorporated Hillsborough County). Coordinates: U.S. Census geocoder match on the operator-published street address.

load_basis: Built capacity: DCD (2023) reports MIA02 at 65,500 sq ft and 6 MW at N+1; operator page gives 9 MW for MIA01 and MIA02 combined

Our inventory carries 21 MW for this fid, more than double the operator's combined figure. A third site (NW 106th St and NW 112th Ave) was reported as planned in 2023; no evidence it operates. Context from the Florida PSC 2025 Ten-Year Site Plan review, Table 3 (https://floridapsc.com/pscfiles/website-files/PDF/Utilities/Electricgas/TenYearSitePlans/2025/Review.pdf): FPL identified 62 existing data center accounts using 283.0 GWh in 2024 (about 32 average MW in total, 30.2 MW summer-peak impact), and the PSC calls Florida's existing data centers 'relatively small'. load_basis: Operator page: 'Site capacity: 6.375 MW' (capacity, not metered draw)
notes: 2850 Interstate Drive, Lakeland; 105,000+ sq ft disaster-recovery and colocation facility. NOT the Six/Ten site in our inventory (bi:1139-0 sits about 15 miles east in Winter Haven), so this is a new site. Utility: the operator page cites 'separate city power redundancy' with dual feeds from two substations, and the address is inside Lakeland city limits, which points to the municipal utility; no document names Lakeland Electric outright, hence medium. Lakeland Electric reported exactly one existing data center to the PSC, using 4.1 GWh in 2024 (about 0.5 average MW) (https://floridapsc.com/pscfiles/website-files/PDF/Utilities/Electricgas/TenYearSitePlans/2025/Review.pdf); if that is this site, actual draw is a small fraction of the 6.375 MW capacity. Opening year not published. Coordinates: U.S. Census geocoder match on the operator-published street address.
